# Numerical appendix template — default for every new appendix

User instruction (2026-11-26): all appendices must be professionally typeset in real LaTeX using the shared maxcut-appendix.sty (STIX2 text and mathematics, A4, 11 pt, consistent margins, restrained running heads, numbered sections, numbered captions, booktabs tables). Do not position page text manually using Matplotlib or fixed PDF overlays. Matplotlib/AwesomeFigures is for figures only; use STIX math fonts and hybrid PDF export, rasterizing heavy artists at 600 dpi, retaining vector labels. Arrange figures close to their captions and interpretations; group related plots on one page when legibility permits. No artificial blank gaps or orphaned captions; use an appropriate full page for dense multi-panel figures. Every report must have a research question, mathematical/protocol definitions, key numerical results, interpretation using the actual audited numbers, limitations and reproducibility notes. Do not invent findings.

Commit the final standalone PDF AND a self-contained LaTeX project (main.tex, reusable style, generated TeX tables, scripts, figure PDFs and compact source summaries, README and provenance hashes) under the experiment's full/latex/ directory. Large raw trajectories, factor archives, iteration/event CSVs and checkpoints stay on the VM with recorded paths and checksums. Individual report figures are now explicitly requested as Git-tracked LaTeX assets; this supersedes the prior PDF-only deliverable rule for these small assets. Do not push raw data or large intermediates merely to publish an appendix.

Use the existing audited data to build the report, no new optimization or repeated full audit solely for layout. Compile via latexmk -pdf -interaction=nonstopmode -halt-on-error main.tex. Verify the actual PDF: embedded STIX2 text/math fonts, no overfull boxes or unresolved references, captions and tables readable, render all pages and inspect a contact sheet plus representative full-size pages. Keep a reproducible build, verify source assets and publication, and serialize final Git writes; never force-push.

Example: Experiment036 (geometry-guided hyperplane rounding) includes all 17 existing figures, actual paired estimates, and a 15-page report. Reuse its structure, not its specific data or conclusions. Use the shared style package; copy it into the self-contained report to freeze layout. New experiment code should generate the TeX tables dynamically from the audited summary.

**Methods overview (required):** Before the primary numerical results, explain every benchmarked method and baseline in plain language, including the basic mathematical idea, proposal/update rule, objective and acceptance/stopping rule when relevant. Use the actual implementation and distinguish geometric surrogates from the original graph objective. Match method names to the tables and figure legends. Place this overview near the beginning of the appendix; never assume readers know the algorithms.
